item.title: C# Method Hiding vs Overriding: Differentiating 'new' and 'override' Keywords
item.description:
“C# Method Hiding vs Overriding: Differentiating ’new’ and ‘override’ Keywords”

Investigating Method Hiding (new keyword) Versus Method Overriding (virtual/override)

The core difference lies in how the runtime resolves the method call, especially when an instance of a derived class is referenced by a base class type.

Scenario 1: Method Hiding (Shadowing with new)

Method hiding uses the new keyword in the derived class to introduce a new method that shares the same signature as a base class method. This new implementation only exists on the derived type. If the base type references the derived object, the base implementation is invoked for non-virtual methods marked with new.

item.title: Python Parent Method Calling Techniques: Super() vs Direct Access
item.description:
“Python Parent Method Calling Techniques: Super() vs Direct Access”

When dealing with inheritance in object-oriented Python programming, a common requirement arises: how does a child class correctly invoke a method defined in its parent class, especially when that method has been overridden? While the super() function is the modern standard, several techniques exist, differing based on Python versions and specific inheritance scenarios (like multiple inheritance). This deep dive examines these diverse approaches for accessing parent functionality.

item.title: JavaScript Inheritance: WeatherWidget Prototype vs. Object.create
item.description:
JavaScript Inheritance: WeatherWidget Prototype vs. Object.create

When implementing inheritance in JavaScript, particularly when trying to mimic class-based structures, developers often encounter different approaches for setting up the prototype chain. A common pattern involves assigning a new instance of a parent constructor to the child’s prototype, such as WeatherWidget.prototype = new Widget;. However, modern JavaScript offers more direct and often preferred methods like Object.create().

Let’s delve into why WeatherWidget.prototype = new Widget; is used and explore its implications, alongside more contemporary solutions for achieving prototype-based inheritance.
